I really wanted to love this trimmer. Especially given the hefty price tag. It trims as you would expect and the vacuum works well and is a must-have feature in my opinion. Another must have feature is either Ni-Mh battery or the more expensive Lithium ion battery. This has Neither it is the bad/cheapo/old Ni-Cad (Nickel Cadmium) with all the memory effects and shortened life span that implies. For a device like this where you can't swap the battery yourself and you can't leave the job half done you will have to partially charge and then finish your trim. Then you will recharge it fully, boom instant battery memory and shortened life. Or maybe you re-charge it after every use? That may be even worse... I've been through this before, you are doomed to a useful life measured in months before the battery (and therefore the whole trimmer) craps out. I researched on line and couldn't discover what type of battery it was so I went in person to my local WM and looked at the packaging, still no hint. So I bought it thinking they couldn't possibly sell it at such a high price point with such an unsuitable battery. I got it home and found in the instructions that the battery is Ni-Cad and soldered into place and must be disposed of properly. I'll be returning it and looking for a different vacuum trimmer with a battery that will be useful for longer than a few months.

I've been wearing extensions for over 15 years- clip ins, tapes, Great Lengths, you name it. I've tried many different brands. I was very excited to try these- based on the reviews and the price. Let me tell you- save your $$. I purchased on the Canadian site where you can see my verified review but wanted to leave this here also to save other people from my misfortune. When they arrived, the hair looked beautiful. It was healthy and shiny looking. I ordered 4 bundles- 16inch, 18inch and 2 packs of 20inch. The 20inches were tied too tight on the tape bonds when they arrived- it left a funny wavy dent that made it impossible to seal properly during installation. Fortunately, it wasn't all of them, but quite a few were un-usable. They were also very thin at the ends, like other reviews stated, and had to be trimmed an inch or two off the bottom to make it look decent. I had an important event coming up and had already booked my appointment to have them professionally installed, so I just cut my losses and ordered another pack of 16inch to make up the difference. So I bought 5 packs in total. All in colour 8/60. When I first had them installed, they looked great. Up until the first wash... I have now had them in for 2 weeks- I just washed them for the 3rd time last night. I know how to care for extensions- I sleep with a silk scarf over them after putting into a loose braid, use only the highest quality products, deep condition below the bond for minimum 30 min after each wash, use minimal heat, and use a good heat protector when I do. After only TWO WEEKS- the hair is garbage (see photo) I will have to take them out. The photo is AFTER I attempted to smooth them out and cut off another inch. They are full of split ends, and look disgusting. I'm wondering if these are even real hair at this point. They feel and look like cheap doll hair. I'm not sure if the other reviews were either written directly after install and not after washing or wearing for even a few days- or if I got a bad batch?? Maybe the darker colours are better. I don't know. All I know is I'm super disappointed and out of pocket over $500 after install. The only good thing I can say is that the tape itself is strong and stayed in.

To begin, I purchase this electric razor because the reviews were good and the price was similar to purchasing replacement HQ9 XL heads for my Norelco electric razor. What I notice was that the Norelco heads sank down into the shaver head which resulted in a large smooth surface for the razor to move across your face. The new shaver heads sank down the same way but did not result in a large smooth surface area moving across my face like the Norelco. So at this point I plan to order a new set of HQ9 heads and look into returning the unit.

[[VIDEOID:3c4d30d8ebacec043d1033906e909174]] I was really excited and happy to buy this Beauty Bon 12 Piece Mani/Pedi set as I've been wanting a set exactly like this one for a long while! Please watch the video as it is absolutely necessary you SEE this 12 piece Beauty Bon Mani/Pedi set on video! I've done a lot of product review videos and this is probably the most important one I've done. If you are looking of a review where someone shares what they wished they would've known BEFORE they bought a really neat looking product, then you must watch this video review and read the written review! I have wanted a mani/pedi set like this that I could pop in my purse because it seems I'm always breaking a nail and don't ever know exactly where my clippers/nail files are. I wouldn't be embarrassed to have this one in my purse, but as you see on the video there were some problems with the case which was the first warning sign that this set might not be all I would want it to be. But then the description contradicts itself and says the kit has a zipper closure. Untrue. If you look at other reviewers' photos in addition to the product photo, this case does NOT have a zipper. Warning flag. As I show you in the video, these mani/pedi pieces are not only poor quality, more than one piece broke upon using it only once. I was so excited to have and use this set and equally disappointed when the set turned out to be so poor in quality. There is one item that I liked and will use: the biggest clipper- though the quality is still sub par. The smaller clipper broke after I clipped a few of my tiny toe nails. The third small clipper with an angled edge didn't work at all. The difference between these clippers and others I've owned is that they don't have resistance and therefore cannot cut the nail. I show you how neither the nipper nor the scissors would cut through my skin. Useless! The nail file is so tiny that it is intended more for if you break a nail and need a nail file in a pinch to smooth a nail on the spot-not as a full mani/pedi set! The tweezers don't work as they can't grab anything. There are several tiny tools which I have used in the past to help with the in-grown toenails I have on my big toes or to clean out under my nails. But the last few are a mystery not only to me but most reviewers who commented on them as I think most were stumped. Some of the mystery pieces looked like what would be in my blemish remover kit. The description starts to list the pieces in this 12 piece set yet doesn't list them all. There is no information about the set and it could use a sheet included that lists he tools and describes what they are used for as obviously we customers don't know and would like to. To put it mildly, I was disappointed that the cuticle nipper that is shown in the product photograph is NOT the nipper that comes with this set. I looked at all the reviewer photographs of their set up to date of this review it seems they also did not get the nipper that is in the photo either. I know the difference because I own a nipper that looks like the one in the photograph and it is much different than the one that came with my set. To add insult to injury- the one that came with my set is not working and broken as you can see in the video. I feel it is defrauding a customer to advertise a product in a photograph representing what the buyer will receive and then do not send exactly what is shown to the customer. And if they do change the product, they should alert the customer before shipping and give them an option to opt out. Look closely and you see tha the nipper in the photo has an extra metal piece on the right handle, but what we as customers have received looks nothing like that. The following product shows what the nipper in the photograph looks like; I expected something similar: [[ASIN:B017N5DMHM Podiatrist's Toenail Clippers for Thick and Ingrown Nails -- Surgical Grade Stainless Steel]]. My one star review is fair. The majority of the pieces in my set don't work. None of the pieces are the quality I would expect at this price level as I expect items to work when I buy them. I think that is a fair expectation.. There is one clipper that works, but the quality is relative to the rest. I don't feel the case is sturdy enough to last very long as it already has issues. For these and the other reasons you can see in the video and written reviews I would not recommend this product. This product was bought at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. AWFUL. I was really hoping this mascara would fill the sad, gaping hole left by the discontinuance of Scandal Queen, which was the most perfect, amazing mascara EVER, but nope, the Quattro Film Type mascara is a hugely over-priced disaster. FIRST: The design sucks. The piece in the tube that's supposed to scrape off excess mascara doesn't work well, so the brush pulls out too much mascara with random blobs of it in places. Then, the brush bristles are waayyy too short, especially for such thick mascara with fibers, so the bristles can't properly pull through your lashes to distribute the mascara and the mascara just kinda blobs on. I included some photos below to try to show the blobs and how short the bristles are, but I'm not sure if you can tell (black mascara on black bristles is hard to photograph). Where there aren't blobs on the brush, the mascara lightly coats the corresponding lashes, resulting in a very uneven, lumpy/chunky application. And you can't even use the brush to try to distribute the mascara through your lashes evenly because there's still too much mascara on it due to the crappy scraper-thing, so if you try to do that, it just globs on more mascara and now you're starting to look like a toddler's puffy paint art project. SECOND: Usually you can even out even the clumpiest mascaras using an eyelash comb after the mascara dries a bit. But not with Quattro because combing it actually pulls off large chunks of the mascara (I think because it's so clumpy/chunky on application, it all sticks together and comes off in pieces). So the length gets all uneven because the fibers lengthen your lashes, but the combing pulls off some of these fibers. And the volume becomes patchy and there are literally gaps in the mascara. There have been a few times where it looked like I had a floating eyelash because black mascara covered half the eyelash, then there was a gap of light-colored natural lash without mascara, and then the mascara continued at the tip of my eyelash. I've never had anything like this happen with mascara. THIRD: I don't know this for sure, but I swear my eyelashes got shorter and thinner because of this mascara. They were very long and thick because I've used GrandeLash and LiLash for a long time, but a couple months after using this Quattro mascara I realized my lashes were noticeably thinner and shorter, even though I was still using LiLash. I was still using this mascara even though I didn't like it because it's SO expensive, but I stopped using it when I realized my lashes looked thinner/shorter. It's only been a couple weeks since I stopped using it so it's too soon to know for sure if it's the mascara. I'm 33 y/o and I've tried A LOT of mascaras, and this is the worst mascara I've EVER used. Most of the mascaras I haven't liked are because they smudge too easily or don't add enough length or volume, but those problems are fixable by adding a second mascara and/or layering. But this mascara is in a class by itself--it's not fixable, causes a mess, and possibly hurts your eyelashes. I don't usually have such strong feelings about a product, but this mascara is THE WORST.

Immediately after purchasing this product, I gave it a four-star review. However, after six months of owning it, I have decided that it is not right for me and am changing my rating. I have watery eyes, oily lids, and long lashes, meaning anything I put on top of the lid is going to end up underneath it in a few hours. After reading hundreds of reviews of vegan, organic liquid liners, I decided to give this one a chance because of all the good reviews. I liked it a lot in some regards, but there were too many drawbacks, which I will detail here. Hopefully this will help you decide if this product is right for you. Pros: - No irritation - Does not smudge or transfer to under eye area, even after exercise (yay!!) - Removes easily with normal facial cleanser (double yay!!) - Very black Cons: - Difficult to apply, even with an expert hand. (I am all about identical, precise cat eyes.) During application, if you lift up the brush once and then try to continue your line, you will find that it scratches into what you have already applied and leaves gaps that need to be covered up with careful dabbing of more product. After three or four applications, I got used to the consistency of the formula, but this is one of the biggest drawbacks of this product. (Also, even though as a whole it comes off very easily at the end of the day, fixing little mistakes with just some water or spit is quite difficult for some reason, perhaps because the product is still tacky.) - The liner does not sink into your skin, meaning it sits on top of your eyelid and will flake off over the course of a day. Miraculously, it doesn't give you raccoon eyes, but it does create a ragged edge or little gaps in your liner that are obvious up close. - Having used various pen, liquid, and gel liners over the years, I find the design of this brush terrible. It is not a bristle brush; it is more of an inflexible point. The design also makes it so you can't grip very closely to the tip, giving you less control. This makes it so you end up with a coat of liner on your lashes (I do have long lashes, for the record). Like I said, the applicator just does not allow a lot of control, especially when you're trying to go back in and fix precise gaps. I appreciate that this product is vegan and organic, but let's be honest... you can't have your cake and eat it, too. I couldn't deal with the frustrations of the application. I ended up tossing this product and purchasing Black Noir Waterproof liner by NYX that is ah-MA-zing. It is everything this product is not, albeit a little more chemical-y.

Oh my word- no. Okay- so this looked like a wonderful beginner kit. I am not a beginner, but I was excited to have everything in a tiny package- something easy to pull out with friends but with high quality results. I got a friend, we opened the box and assumed I'd be ready to do her nails without getting my nail kit. Nope. The first sept (as it always is) was to clean buff and shape the nail- nothing included to do that. I thought- okay- no big deal. I got my stuff out and took care of it. I then applied their prep product- Nail dehydrator- all good. I started to plug in the nail light, so I’d be ready after we apply the first coat- but this kit didn't include a plug- just a usb cord. (sigh) I got up again- and got an extra usb plug I had. Now slightly annoyed because this is supposed to be a ready kit- but hey-- really-- not a huge deal. Then I applied the base coat. Whew- runny. I wasn’t impressed with it’s consentaneity. But maybe it’d perform well? Then I tried to cure it. Cue the light-- Oh, my word their nail lamp is horrible. It’s very cheap looking- only fits four fingers- not the thumb at the same time, and really feels off- like the break into shards plastic, not the bendy kind. (I was still trying to accept this as a no big deal point but the red flags were slapping me in the face.) I read the pamphlet to see how long it needed to cure- the pamphlet said "cure for the appropriate time" or something just a vague. I read the nail polish, to find the appropriate time- nope. I looed over the box- nothing. We used the lamp like 5 times and finally got her base coat cured. Then we had to do the same with just her thumb. I have nail lights that cost three bucks that work better than this thing. I’m not kidding. In fact- I use single nail lights that only cure one nail at a time—and this was SLOWER! Okay- that was over. Where is the red polish? The box says: “Step two apply polish” and it has a picture of the polish- a red polish, they name it like it’s included. It’s not. This starter kit isn’t much of a START without a polish- but Okay- my nail kit to save the day. I pulled out a blush pink gel that always does me right. But the base coat is weird. The polish is almost clumping on the nail. It applies a tad bit patchy. I get that not all formulas work together—but they DIDN’T GIVE ME a polish to work with so theirs- in theory- should be mostly universal. I didn’t know I was intended to buy-one polishe- AND their kit to make this happen. I try to cure MY gel polish tin their lamp. (thank goodness my friend is a very laid-back person- she was amazing about this, laughing with me--) I was itching to pull out a good lamp but I didn’t, so I’d give this a true test. (Or because I wanted to test my patience. Two birds one stone) Now—here is the saving grace— the top coat is wonderful. It works like some of my best top coats- it leaves that perfect glassy look and it applies like a dream. Later I used the same top coat on my nails- and it worked just as well without the weird base coat and the horrible lamp and a totally different brand of nail polish. THIS WHOLE KIT AND THE ONLY THING THEY HAVE GOING FOR IT IS THE TOP COAT! Now I get why this has good reviews—it’s the gel top coat. No wonder it lasts- I can only guess Red Carpet knows their top coat is fantastic, so they threw a bunch of bad apples in here –aware beginners won’t know any better. Please. You can buy wonderful topcoats for 10-20 bucks NOT 50 OF YOUR HARD-EARNED DOLLARS- This is such a sad waste- and they don’t even throw in a file, or a plug in or red polish? I have more stuff coming from this brand—things I got before I tried this-- that I’m going to be trying- I really hope this is their only issue... we shall see.  I hope this review was helpful because I don’t want your money wasted. :(

I would not have bought these had I known this as my wife reacts to polyester. This just leaves me with another useless set of eye covers that my wife can't use. Also, I personally find these uncomfortable. The silk is nothing like my nice soft silk shirts. It is still a shiny and smooth fabric, yet also an uncomfortably rough (I'm not sure how better to describe it -- it's like running your skin over tiny closely spaced wires), fabric that is very hot to wear on your face. Furthermore, I found that I got a headache both times I tried wearing these. My wife has previously made some passable eye-covers out of cotton socks that we both can wear -- and I find significantly more comfortable. She's suggested that maybe she can try taking these apart and using the straps and cotton parts and making better cotton-sock eye-covers. I'm skeptical and am considering returning these. I'm certainly not happy. If you like the really slick-abrasive feeling fabrics like cheap silks or cheap satins, and if you don't have any issue with the polyester in these, I can't really see a problem with them. They could probably benefit from being a bit larger, but they're 'pillowy'-enough (for lack of a better word) to block out most of the light and fill in the gaps around the edges. Mystery as to why they give me a headache, but they've enough good reviews that it can't be common. I'm giving them 2 stars because I think the description is misleading and I don't like them, but also because I think a more moderate rating would get this lost among rating of people who are happy with the item. I was excited to try this scrub once I started reading some of its many positive reviews. I even signed up for auto-delivery. But then I received my first delivery and tried it. I’m confused about how this has so many positive reviews. This is the worst body scrub I’ve ever tried, by far! I typically love body scrubs whether they’re based w/ sugar, salt, coffee, or just about any exfoliant! I’m not a scrub snob either - I’ve tried tons of different brands and “flavors” and can’t say I have one clear favorite. I’ve used and loved niche natural brands from health food stores, ritzy expensive spa-type brands from dept stores and boutiques, and cheap brands from the drugstore equally. I’ve used scrubs that cost $48 for a smallish tub (yikes!) but had just as excellent results from ones that cost $5 for a huge tub of the stuff. I’ve used brands that rinsed clean and other brands that were so oily I had to use a wooden spoon to stir the separated oils back in to the mixture. I found some quality I liked about every scrub I can remember trying - until this one. This scrub has natural ingredients and I love that! But aside from that I don’t see any real advantages or benefits to this product. I swear my container of this scrub had the oddest consistency I’ve ever encountered! It was like an important ingredient was missing because this was like a tub of flaky, dry salt or sugar. I actually started trying to dig deep into the tub to mix the product, erroneously thinking maybe there was a layer of oil or moisture in the bottom of the container. There wasn’t. It’s just a tub of sandy, dry bits. Period. This product didn’t moisturize at all and it wasn’t even particularly smoothing. I had a hard time patting it on my wet/damp skin, truth be told. Again, I’ve tried scrubs that were on the drier side and enjoyed them. But this was bone dry! I think scrubbing myself with the contents of a sugar bowl would’ve been more effective. This didn’t exfoliate well, had zero moisturizing properties, and had no scent, pleasant or otherwise. It was a disappointing, very odd waste of money and time. I immediately canceled my subscribe and save subscription. Big thanks to Amazon for making THAT part easy, at least. And I’m also very relieved I bought this for what’s listed as the “sale price” as opposed to the laughable, listed suggested retail price. I’ll NEVER buy this again and will avoid the brand as a whole.
